text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton, citing "severe repression", in Burma, has formally imposed economic sanctions on Rangoon, including a ban on U.S. investment in its oil and natural gas development.
- Home upgraders in Singapore out-numbered downgraders in the ratio of two to one between 1991 and 1995.

- he Federal Reserve left the overnight bank lending rate unchanged at 5.5 percent, though a rate increase is still possible in the months ahead if the central banks' bet on slower growth does not pan out.
- Share prices on regional bourses rose following the Fed's decision not to raise its key interest rate.
- Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Virawan said he wanted interest rates cut to boost the flagging economy, as industry sources said a discount rate cut was already in the works.

- The Thai stock exchange is cracking down on chronic loss-makers. It has warned 20 companies they face delisting, and put their senior management and majority shareholders on notice that they will be blacklisted unless they take steps to rehabilitate their companies.
- Federal Reserve inflation fighters held their fire by leaving interest rates unchanged, buoying U.S. asset markets, but sparking criticism from some economists on Wall Street.
- Long lines formed at Hong Kong banks as investors scrambled to apply for shares in Beijing Enterprises Holdings, the latest mainland firm to lauch a public offering in the territory.
- Top executives of Credit Lyonnais looted the bank through "organised financial fraud" up to 1993, according to allegations in a confidential document published by a French newspaper.
